summary: 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard (Mission Bay Block 26A) is a 6-story office building in Mission Bay, developed as ML Mission Bay LLC with Swinerton Builders as general contractor per the project's precast contractor's own page, which -- together with DataSF Assessor records -- dates its completion to 2008.

milestones.text: SF Dept. of Building Inspection permit #200705030366 filed for a temporary tower crane "for construction of 6 story building" at this address

images.credit: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency, NAIP aerial imagery (2024 flight), via USDA's 'latest NAIP' image service

Read 2026-09-22.
images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

sources.title: Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls (blklot 8721010, 500 Terry A. Francois Blvd): year_property_built 2008
Building Permits: permit #200705030366 (500 Terry A. Francois, block 8721 lot 001 at filing), filed 2007-05-03, "temporary tower crane for construction of 6 story building", completed 2008-04-24
sources.publisher: DataSF / SF Department of Building Inspection

open_questions: Exact month/day of the 2008 completion is not sourced, only the year.

The 2007 crane permit's own block/lot (block 8721, lot 001) differs from the lot the Assessor now uses for this address (lot 010); the address and 2008-04-24 permit-completion date (matching the Assessor's 2008 year) line up with this parcel, so this is treated as a lot renumbering, not a different building.

The building's architect and its later Cisco/Meraki tenant history are documented elsewhere (this project's own geometry file cites the SF Chronicle for the Meraki lease) but were not independently re-verified in this minimal-dossier pass, so are left out here rather than repeated unsourced.
